records.name: Philadelphia Dragon Boat Association
records.summary: The city's dragon boat racing club, founded in 1983, that trains on the Schuylkill and brings in newcomers through a rookie program that starts in June.
records.what_you_do: Paddle in early morning practices, try rookie sessions with loaner paddles and life jackets, and race in regattas.

schedule.text: High performance practices five mornings a week, April through September, starting at 5:45 AM. Rookie sessions begin once a week in June after the Independence Dragon Boat Regatta, with weeknight rookie practices planned for 2026.

locations.label: Schuylkill River dock in Fairmount Park

cost.text: Dues are not listed on the pages read. Rookie sessions provide loaner paddles, seat pads and life jackets.

first_step.how: Fill out the interest form on the recruiting page. The club says it replies within 72 hours.
first_step.basis: The club runs rookie sessions with loaner gear and says how a newcomer starts.

records.notes: Pages carry a 'Public Beta Version, February 2026' label, so details may shift. No street address for the dock was on the pages read. The June Independence Dragon Boat Regatta is an annual festival the club runs; it is not recorded as a separate group.

records.name: Pennsylvania Dragon Boat Club
records.summary: A nonprofit dragon boat club with a recreational side and a race team, paddling the Schuylkill on weekend mornings. Recreational paddlers can come about once a month.
records.what_you_do: Paddle on the Schuylkill on Thursday, Saturday and Sunday mornings in season, run on Tuesday evenings, and race at regattas.

schedule.text: Team practices Thursday, Saturday and Sunday mornings during the dragon boat season on the Schuylkill River. Runs Tuesday evenings, sometimes at the Temple track.

cost.text: Membership fees are not listed. The site has a donation button only.

first_step.how: Email penndbc@gmail.com or use the contact form on penndbc.com.
first_step.basis: A Join page exists, but it gives no sign up steps, so the way in is not clear.

records.notes: The site lists a 2026 staff roster but no dated events or races, so the status is inferred from a working site. Its events section is linked but showed no dates.

records.name: Crescent Boat Club
records.summary: A rowing club founded in 1867 on Boathouse Row. It teaches people to row from the start in a Novice Camp and runs a youth rowing program.
records.what_you_do: Learn to scull in the Novice Camp, move on to the scullers development program, or join junior racing. Members keep boats in club storage.

schedule.text: Summer rowing programs run each year. The 2025 summer programs were posted in May 2025; 2026 dates were not found.

cost.text: Annual dues and registration fees apply. Amounts are not listed on the page read.

first_step.how: Start from the membership and contact section of crescentboatclub.org. The page lists no phone or email.
first_step.basis: Novice Camp teaches beginners, but dues and a membership step come first, and no direct contact is listed.

records.notes: The newest dated post is May 2025, so the status is probably_active rather than active. The safety page lists 842 Kelly Drive as an emergency address, which differs from the 5 Kelly Drive boathouse address. Confirm before publish.

records.name: Philadelphia City Rowing
records.summary: A free after school program for Philadelphia public and charter school students. It pairs competitive rowing with academic support, mentoring and wellness lessons.
records.what_you_do: Row on a team, get help with schoolwork, and take part in mentoring and wellness education.

schedule.text: After school programming for students who attend Philadelphia public or charter schools. Days and hours were not on the pages read.

records.notes: The group's own site (philadelphiacityrowing.org) returned HTTP 403 and was not read, so the sign up route, locations and schedule are unknown. Facts come from a July 3, 2026 NBC10 article about a $50,000 grant, which said it serves over 400 students a year. Check the group's own site before publish. Verdict is publish only on the strength of the news item.

records.name: Fairmount Rowing Association
records.summary: A rowing club founded in 1877 on Boathouse Row, known for masters rowing for adults. It also runs a summer rowing program for junior rowers.
records.what_you_do: Adults row masters sculls and sweep boats and take part in club social events. Young rowers join the summer juniors program.

schedule.text: A summer rowing program for juniors, with 2026 program information posted. Practice times for adults were not listed.

cost.text: Membership fees and program prices are not on the pages read.

first_step.how: Use the membership section of fairmountrowing.org or contact the club. The site shows a phone label with no number.
first_step.basis: Membership is the way in, and the site does not describe a beginner program.

records.notes: Linked news items are titled Quaker City 2026 info and FRA Summer 2026 Program Information, but the page showed no dates, so the month of last activity is unknown. The Boathouse Row adult page lists Fairmount with no adult lesson details.

records.name: Penn Athletic Club Rowing
records.summary: The rowing program of Penn Athletic Club on Boathouse Row. It runs adult Learn to Row classes that are open to the public, masters rowing, and junior learn to row programs.
records.what_you_do: Try rowing in an adult Learn to Row class, then move on to masters rowing for fitness or racing.

locations.label: Penn Athletic Club rowing boathouse, Boathouse Row

cost.text: Class cost and schedule are not on the page read.

first_step.how: Use the Contact Us page at pennac.org/contact. The page lists no phone or email.
first_step.basis: Adult Learn to Row is open to the public, but the page gives no class times, prices or sign up steps.

records.notes: The home page has no dated news. A learn to row sub page was not found at the guessed address. Membership rules for Learn to Row are unstated.

records.name: Vesper Boat Club
records.summary: A competitive rowing club on Boathouse Row with a racing team for post college rowers, a masters racing program, and a summer camp for rowers under 23.
records.what_you_do: Train year round in big boats, race at local regattas, or join masters racing.

schedule.text: Year round practices for the racing team. A three month summer camp for athletes under 23.

cost.text: Fees are not listed on the page read.

first_step.how: Use the Contact page on vesperboatclub.org. No phone or email is shown.
first_step.basis: The programs are for specific groups of racers (post college sweep rowers, masters, athletes under 23), and the path in is not described.

records.notes: Dated news runs to October 5, 2026, including a Vesper Erg Derby series. This is a racing club, so it is a fit for experienced or masters rowers rather than complete beginners.

records.name: Philadelphia Girls Rowing Club
records.summary: A women's rowing club on Boathouse Row that trains adult novices in a yearly program and pairs each new rower with a mentor.
records.what_you_do: Learn to row on machines and then on the river, pass a skills and safety test, and help with the club's main fundraiser, the Braxton Regatta.

schedule.text: A yearly novice training program. An information session for applicants is held once a year in late April. Class dates are not listed.

cost.text: The adult novice program costs $950 in total: $600 in dues and a $350 initiation fee, due on the first day of training.

first_step.how: Send a letter or email to pgrcmembers14@gmail.com saying why you want to join and what rowing experience you have. Applicants may be invited to the spring information session.
first_step.basis: Applicants must apply, may be invited to a session, and pay a fixed fee. Physical requirements apply: lift and carry a boat, and be able to swim.

records.notes: The older .com address redirects to the .org site. The how to join page lists no dated events; the status is inferred from a working site. The club asks applicants for a home address and phone number, which are not recorded here.

records.name: Bachelors Barge Club
records.summary: A rowing club on Boathouse Row that says it welcomes both experienced and new rowers, with group and private coaching that can teach beginners.
records.what_you_do: Row with coaches on the Schuylkill, take group or private coaching, or come back to rowing after college.

locations.label: Bachelors Barge Club boathouse, Boathouse Row

cost.text: Pricing is on a separate page that was not read.

first_step.how: Find the Membership and Pricing pages on bachelorsbargeclub.org. The contact details on the home page look like template placeholders, so none are recorded.
first_step.basis: The club says coaches teach beginners, but membership and prices are on pages not read, and no working contact was found.

records.notes: The home page shows a placeholder address (123 Street Avenue), a 555 phone number and an example email, so it may be an unfinished site. Verify the club is active before publish. No dated items found.

records.name: University Barge Club
records.summary: A rowing club founded in 1854 on Boathouse Row. It offers recreational rowing at your own pace and a masters team that races in local regattas.
records.what_you_do: Row for fitness and friends at your own pace, or join the masters team at regattas such as the Head of the Schuylkill.

locations.label: University Barge Club boathouse, Boathouse Row

cost.text: Fees are not listed on the page read.

first_step.how: Use the contact page at universitybargeclub.com/contact. The page shows no phone or email.
first_step.basis: The site does not describe how to join or any beginner option.

records.notes: No upcoming or dated events on the site. The page notes that rowing stops when river flow on the USGS gauge exceeds 18,000 cubic feet per second.

records.name: Malta Boat Club
records.summary: A rowing club on Boathouse Row, founded in 1860, that is open to anyone interested in the sport. Members row socially or race, coach and volunteer at Philadelphia rowing events.
records.what_you_do: Row socially, use the erg and weight room, or volunteer, officiate or coach at Schuylkill Navy and city rowing events.

cost.text: Dues are not listed on the page read.

first_step.how: Call (215) 769-9030 or visit 9 Boathouse Row. The site lists no dues or sign up steps.
first_step.basis: Membership is open to anyone and a phone number is listed, but the site does not describe a beginner program.

records.notes: The only date on the site is the 2026 copyright footer, which is not evidence of activity. Status is inferred from a working site with no dated news.

records.name: Undine Barge Club
records.summary: A rowing club founded in 1856 on Boathouse Row. It runs masters and high performance rowing, a U23 summer program and team rowing opportunities.
records.what_you_do: Join a masters, high performance or U23 summer program, or look into the club's team rowing opportunities.

cost.text: Fees are not listed on the page read.

first_step.how: Use the Becoming a Member page at undine.com, or call (215) 765-9244.
first_step.basis: The club lists membership and team programs, but no beginner course and no eligibility rules are described.

records.notes: News items on the site have no dates, and the calendar page contents were not shown.

records.name: Pennsylvania Center for Adapted Sport
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs sport, recreation and wellness programs for people with disabilities. Its programs include adapted rowing, indoor rowing and youth rowing on Boathouse Row.
records.what_you_do: Row on the river with the club's equipment and instruction, or volunteer for the adaptive rowing program.

locations.label: Pennsylvania Center for Adapted Sport, Boathouse Row

cost.text: Program fees are not stated. The site says equipment, venues, instruction and training are provided to participants.

first_step.how: Use the Contact page or the eligibility document on centeronline.com. No phone or email is listed.
first_step.basis: Programs are open to people with disabilities, with a published eligibility document and a volunteer link, but no direct contact details.

records.notes: The site does not use the name Philadelphia Adaptive Rowing, which a search summary attached to this program. Treat that name as unconfirmed. The only dated mentions are a Cinco de Mayo event and a garden cleanup, with no years.

records.name: Head of the Schuylkill Regatta Volunteers
records.summary: The volunteer crew that runs Philadelphia's Head of the Schuylkill Regatta, now in its 56th year. Volunteers help with timing, docks, registration, parking and more.
records.what_you_do: Work half day shifts around lunchtime in timing, docks, registration, parking, hospitality or the zero waste team. Timing volunteers get training.

schedule.text: Shifts run in half days around lunchtime on regatta weekend. Volunteer sign ups open after August 1, 2026. A general information session on Zoom is set for Tuesday, October 20, 2026.

cost.text: No fee is listed for volunteers.

first_step.how: Pick a shift on SignUpGenius after August 1, 2026, or email volunteers@hosr.org. Attend the October 20, 2026 Zoom information session.
first_step.basis: The page welcomes new volunteers, timing needs no rowing experience, training is provided, and it says how to start.

records.notes: The page does not state the 2026 regatta date. Golf cart drivers must be 18 or older with a license, and launch drivers need outboard experience. Independence Day Regatta and Schuylkill Navy Run volunteer sign ups run through Regatta Central and are not recorded here as they are single events.

records.name: Philadelphia Fins Aquatics Club
records.summary: A masters swim team founded in 1988 for LGBTQ+ swimmers, welcoming everyone from first time competitors to record holders.
records.what_you_do: Swim weeknight and weekend workouts at an indoor pool, with or without racing in masters meets.

schedule.text: Monday to Thursday 7:30 to 8:45 pm. Saturday and Sunday 10:30 am to 12 noon.

cost.text: Dues and drop in fees are not listed.

first_step.how: Use the contact form on the club's USMS page or email finsmemberatlarge2@gmail.com. The contact form asks whether you are a USMS member.
first_step.basis: The club welcomes first time swimmers, but USMS registration is part of joining and the page does not explain the cost.

records.notes: The USMS club page lists no dated events, so status is inferred from a working page. The club page does not state a minimum age. A 2025 event listing placed summer workouts at Kelly Pool in Fairmount Park; that aggregator was not used as a source.

notes: Searches used: 8 of 10. Fetches: about 36 of 60. Dropped with reason: Sedgeley Club (women's social club on Boathouse Row; its only dated item is a 2022 caption and no current program was found); Hines Rowing Center, Conshohocken Rowing Center and Whitemarsh Boat Club (outside the city and none says it serves Philadelphia residents); Philadelphia Youth Regatta (single event, not a group). Searches for sailing returned only Center City and Chesapeake clubs; no public sailing community was confirmed on a group page. No swim or rowing group marked 'active' rests on a group's own undated page alone. Several records are low confidence because the sites show no dates or contact methods. Philadelphia City Rowing is the weakest record: its own site was blocked, so the facts come from one July 2026 news article and should be verified before the owner relies on it.
